explanations.explanation: Shinar it is, friend. The people find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Nobody's arguing about the address yet, so that part of the story is smooth sailing. Hold onto that name, because this plain is where the whole story happens.

Goshen is a real place in the Bible, but it's not where this crowd lands. The text says they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there (Genesis 11:2). Goshen shows up later in the Bible, so your memory is working, it just grabbed the wrong map pin. Happens to me with the kitchen drawer where I keep the spatula.

Moab is a good guess, but it's not the one here. The people journeying eastward find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Moab is a different place with its own stories. This group set up camp in Shinar, and that's where the bricks start piling up.

Stone is right, baker. The text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Brick took the place of stone, and tar took the place of mortar. Swapping the whole building kit, that's some bold shopping.

Wood sounds sensible, but it's not in the verse. The text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Their baked bricks stood in for stone. Wood never makes the list in this passage.

Straw is a fair guess, since straw and bricks go together in your head. But this verse never mentions it. It says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Stone is the one the bricks replaced.

explanations.answer: To make a name for themselves
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. They say, “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) They want the name, plain and simple. I think a name that big takes a lot of bricks.

explanations.answer: To guard the plain from enemies
explanations.explanation: Nice thinking, but no enemies show up in this passage. The people say the city and tower are so “that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Guarding the plain never comes up. Their reason is about a name.

That's a clever guess, with the flood just behind them. But the text gives a different reason. They say, “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) A flood watch isn't in the plan.

True, friend. In the same breath as making a name, they say they build so they will “not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Two goals, one tower. Keep that line in your pocket, because it comes back at the end.

Close, but it's true. The people say they build “that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Not being scattered is right there in their plan. It's easy to read past with that tower stealing the spotlight.

explanations.answer: Nothing they plan will be out of their reach
explanations.explanation: Right on, baker. The LORD says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) One people, one language, and whatever they plan is within reach. That's a whole lot of teamwork, and the text says it plainly.

explanations.answer: Their city will grow too big for the plain
explanations.explanation: That's a creative guess, but the LORD never says it. He says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) The point is about what they can plan, not how much room they have. The plain stays out of it.

explanations.answer: Their tower will fall before it is finished
explanations.explanation: I get the guess, but the LORD doesn't say that. He says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) No collapsing tower is mentioned anywhere in this passage. What He does say is about their plans.

That's it, friend. The LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) The plan is about their speech. Bricks and tower stay out of it.

Good guess, since the tower is the big thing in the picture. But the LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) The text doesn't say He brings the tower down. The language is what He goes after.

I can see why you'd say it, all those bricks sitting there. But the LORD's words are, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) Not one brick gets broken in His plan. Language is the target.

Not quite, baker. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) They stopped. Nobody kept laying bricks after that.

False is right, friend. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) The building ended. I think a crew that can't understand each other has a hard time passing the tar.

Babel, baker, you've got it. The text says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) The name comes from what happened there. It's a name that stuck.

Nineveh is a real city in the Bible, but not this one. The text says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) Nineveh is a different place with a different story. This place is called Babel.

Erech is a real place, and it's even named in Genesis 10:10, so you've been paying attention. But this verse says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) Babel is the name for the spot where the language got confused.
